questions.knowledge_point: Finding Critical Points and Then Classifying Them Using the Second Derivative Test
questions.problem:
For the function $f(x)=6{x}^{2}-4{x}^{3},$ which of the following statements are true?

I. ${f}^{″}(0)<0$

II. $x=0$ is a relative minimum of $f(x)$

III. ${f}^{″}(1)>0$

IV. $x=1$ is a relative maximum of $f(x)$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to identify the critical points. Then, we then need to classify them using the second derivative test.

First, we need to identify the critical points. Differentiating $f(x)=6{x}^{2}-4{x}^{3},$ we get

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=12x-12{x}^{2},
$$

and solving ${f}^{′}(x)=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}12x-12{x}^{2} & =0 \\ 12x(1-x) & =0 \\ x & =0,1.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have critical points at $x=0,1.$

Next, we need to determine the sign of ${f}^{″}(x)$ at the critical points. Computing ${f}^{″}(x),$ we get

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=12-24x,
$$

and evaluating ${f}^{″}(x)$ at each critical point, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(0) & =12>0 \\ {f}^{″}(1) & =-12<0.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that:

- Statement I is false while statement II is true. The second derivative is positive at $x=0,$ so this is a relative minimum of $f(x).$

- Statement III is false while statement VI is true. The second derivative is negative at $x=1,$ so this is a relative maximum of $f(x).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and IV only".
